_about: The Focus Group crew. Generic on purpose: {THING} is what the project is (tabletop RPG, Canasta, online debate...), {HOST} is the person who runs a session (DM, dealer, moderator...). The conductor fills these in per project. Names are placeholders: rename freely. Edit here, then run tools/build.py.

testers.name: Pat
testers.who: Has never played {THING} or used anything like this app. Got sent a link or a QR code by a friend.
testers.tech: Average phone user. Will not read instructions.
testers.patience: About two minutes before deciding it's 'not for me'.
testers.first_move: Taps the biggest button on the screen and hopes.
testers.delights: Being told exactly what to do next. Getting a small win in the first minute.
testers.quits: Jargon with no explanation, a blank screen, or any moment of 'wait, what do I do now?'
testers.finds: Onboarding gaps, unexplained terms, dead ends, anything that assumes you already know.
testers.voice: Honest and a little lost. 'I don't know what a {HOST} is.'
testers.origin: Pat from the Demo Weekend cast.

testers.name: Duke
testers.who: Has played {THING} a little but is running or hosting it for the first time. Nervous, wants to look good in front of friends.
testers.tech: Comfortable with apps, new to the {HOST} side of things.
testers.patience: Medium. Will push through if he can see it'll make him look competent.
testers.first_move: Looks for a setup wizard, a template, or a 'quick start'.
testers.delights: Guard rails, presets, and an undo button when he messes up in front of everyone.
testers.quits: Setup that takes longer than the session, or getting embarrassed mid-game by the tool.
testers.finds: Host-side setup pain, missing defaults, no recovery from mistakes, confusing controls under pressure.
testers.voice: Earnest, slightly panicked. 'Okay, how do I let everyone in?'
testers.origin: Duke, the first-time DM from the Demo Weekend cast.

testers.name: Nadia
testers.who: Power user. Has used every serious app or tool for {THING} and knows the best features of each.
testers.tech: Expert. Keyboard shortcuts, settings menus, the works.
testers.patience: High, but zero patience for missing features the competitors already have.
testers.first_move: Opens settings, then tries to do something advanced right away.
testers.delights: Depth, shortcuts, customization, and features she hasn't seen anywhere else.
testers.quits: A ceiling: the moment she can't do what she does in her current tool.
testers.finds: Missing power features, slow workflows, competitor gaps, limits on how far it scales.
testers.voice: Fast, precise, compares everything. 'The other one lets me do this in two clicks.'
testers.origin: Nadia, the VTT power user from the Demo Weekend cast.

testers.name: Grizz
testers.who: Forty-plus years of {THING} in real life, at real tables. Deep expertise, weak with computers.
testers.tech: Low. Big fonts, fewer menus, please. Distrusts anything that hides the rules.
testers.patience: High for the {THING}, low for the technology.
testers.first_move: Tries to do it the way he's always done it at the table.
testers.delights: When the app gets out of the way and respects how {THING} is really played.
testers.quits: When the app forces a video-game way of doing something that works fine in real life, or gets a rule wrong.
testers.finds: Rule mistakes, video-game assumptions that don't fit real play, tiny text, and anything that slows the table down.
testers.voice: Gruff, been-there. 'That's not how anybody actually plays.'
testers.origin: The 40+ year DM tester clone and Grizz from the Demo Weekend cast.

testers.name: Sam
testers.who: Grabbed off the sidewalk. No interest in {THING}, average computer user, here because someone asked.
testers.patience: Low. Polite, but checking their phone.
testers.first_move: Asks 'so what is this?' and waits for the screen to answer.
testers.delights: Instantly understanding what it's for. Something that looks fun before they know how it works.
testers.quits: If they can't explain what the app does after thirty seconds.
testers.finds: Unclear purpose, weak first impressions, anything that only makes sense to fans.
testers.voice: Blunt and unimpressed. 'Okay, but what's the point?'
testers.origin: The never-played tester clone and Sam from the Demo Weekend cast.

testers.name: Dale
testers.who: Loves {THING} but has kids, a job, and forty-five minutes after bedtime. Plays in bursts.
testers.tech: Solid. Used to be hardcore, now just tired.
testers.patience: Good, but every minute of setup is a minute not playing.
testers.first_move: Looks for 'continue where I left off'.
testers.delights: Jumping straight back in, saving progress anywhere, and getting a real session done in short bursts.
testers.quits: Long setup, lost progress, or anything that needs a whole evening.
testers.finds: Resume and save problems, slow startup, sessions that can't be paused, missing reminders of what happened last time.
testers.voice: Warm, wry, practical. 'Can I pause this if the baby wakes up?'

testers.name: Kai
testers.who: Grew up on video games. Fast, mobile-first, compares everything to the games they play.
testers.tech: Very high on phones, impatient with desktop-style menus.
testers.first_move: Mashes through everything and tries to break it.
testers.delights: Speed, flashy feedback, unlocks, and finding a trick nobody intended.
testers.quits: Slow loading, walls of text, or anything that feels 'old'.
testers.finds: Exploits, double-tap and spam bugs, mobile layout problems, missing feedback, and video-game ideas worth stealing.
testers.voice: Fast and blunt. 'Why can't I just swipe it?'
testers.origin: Kai, the video-game-minded player from the Demo Weekend cast.

testers.name: Jax
testers.who: Plays {THING} live for an audience. The app is part of the show, and chat is watching every mistake.
testers.tech: High. Runs OBS, overlays, multiple monitors.
testers.patience: Low for anything that looks bad or stalls on stream.
testers.first_move: Checks how it looks on a stream layout and whether viewers can follow along.
testers.delights: Big readable moments, spectator views, things chat can react to or join, and clips worth sharing.
testers.quits: Tiny text, dead air, loading screens, or anything that embarrasses them live.
testers.finds: Readability at stream size, spectator and audience features, clip-worthy moments, and stalls that would kill a stream.
testers.voice: Performer energy, talks to chat. 'Chat, this is either amazing or I'm about to get ratioed.'
